summary: Created an SSH CA on node1, signed the host's ed25519 key into a certificate, configured sshd to present it via HostCertificate, diagnosed and fixed an SELinux mislabeling issue that initially blocked sshd from loading the cert, and verified end-to-end that a client trusting only the CA key (no pinned host key) connects successfully. Performed the mandatory single-node restart, confirming the boot identity changed and all state (sshd, certificate config, CA-trust connectivity) recovered afterward.
actions_performed: Captured baseline: sshd active, existing host keys, boot_id/machine-id on node1 (cmd-5e2a1ad4104043a2)
Generated ED25519 SSH CA keypair at /etc/ssh/ca/ssh_ca on node1
Signed the host's ssh_host_ed25519_key.pub with the CA (ssh-keygen -s -h, principals node1/NODE_NAME/NODE_IP/localhost, 10y validity) into /etc/ssh/ssh_host_ed25519_key-cert.pub
Configured /etc/ssh/sshd_config with HostCertificate and HostKey directives, validated with sshd -t, restarted sshd (cmd-c529a913d0da46ec)
Diagnosed failure: sshd logged 'Could not load host certificate' because the cert file had SELinux context tmp_t instead of sshd_key_t (cmd-1012b120022e4ad6, cmd-17faa2ae00054854)

Fixed SELinux labeling via restorecon and restarted sshd; confirmed via ssh -vv that the server now offers ssh-ed25519-cert-v01@openssh.com and a client with only a @cert-authority line in known_hosts (no pinned host key) accepts and matches it (cmd-f3984e6548b64f22)
Ran a full authenticated SSH connection using CA-trust-only known_hosts plus the cluster keypair, confirming successful connect without host-key pinning (cmd-a78e7571de4049c1)
Captured pre-restart boot_id and healthy sshd/certificate state (cmd-62fa3b9d65be49bc)
Issued sudo systemctl reboot on node1, backgrounded so the acknowledgement returned before disconnect (cmd-e6a2cc1719954fe4)
Polled node1: first poll timed out (node down) (cmd-13f04eaa7e4149dc), second poll succeeded with a new boot_id, proving the restart occurred (cmd-3729cf5539ca4f6b)

Post-restart verification: sshd active, HostCertificate/HostKey config intact, cert file present with correct SELinux context, and a fresh CA-trust-only SSH client connection succeeded (cmd-ecdb5806a797422d)

evidence.requirement: SSH CA created and host certificate generated and installed on node1
evidence.summary: CA keypair generated, host ed25519 key signed into a 10-year host certificate with correct principals, sshd configured with HostCertificate/HostKey and restarted

evidence.requirement: Client connects trusting only the CA, without pinning the host key
evidence.summary: Initial attempt failed due to SELinux mislabeling (tmp_t) blocking sshd from loading the cert; after restorecon fix, ssh -vv debug output shows the server offering the ed25519 cert and the client (with only a @cert-authority line, no pinned host key) matching and trusting it; a full authenticated connection succeeded end-to-end
Captured boot_id dfdea52d..., sshd active, and certificate still valid/served before reboot

evidence.requirement: Node1 restart acknowledgement and changed boot identity
evidence.summary: systemctl reboot acknowledged and backgrounded before disconnect; node unreachable on first poll, then reachable with a new boot_id (4d100cc9...), proving a real restart

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of services, certificate config, and CA-trust connectivity
evidence.summary: After reboot: sshd active, HostCertificate/HostKey directives intact, cert file present with correct SELinux context, and a fresh SSH connection using only CA-trust known_hosts succeeded
